text:
From planting to emergence (VE) and the first true leaves (V2), successful germination depends on adequate soil moisture and temperature (soil temperature above about 21°C supports faster, more even emergence). Under good conditions, germination and emergence take roughly 5-7 days. The radicle (root) emerges first, then the coleoptile pushes the shoot up through the soil, protecting the first leaf until it reaches the surface.

Cold soil, soil crusting, seed planted too deep, or dry topsoil can each slow emergence or cause uneven stands. Because this stage sets the final plant population for the season, uniform, timely emergence across the field is an important management goal -- see the planting depth and seeding rate topic for practical guidance.
